title: RY-Tau
caption: The stellar nursery around RY Tau, imaged by the Gemini North telescope
celestial: RY Tau · constellation Taurus · about 450 light-years away (source figure)
credit: International Gemini Observatory/Club d’astronomie de Dorval/Stephanie Cote, Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics/Travis Rector, University of Alaska, Anchorage

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Wispy remains of a gas cloud trail around a bright star at the bottom center of this Gemini North image of RY Tau, a stellar nursery. That cloud is the one that formed the star, and the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) shows its wisps in fine detail.

The system lies approximately 140 parsecs, or 450 light-years, away in Taurus, and spans roughly two-thirds of a light-year. The central star is a variable star whose visual brightness wanders between magnitudes 9 and 11 on no regular schedule. On the magnitude scale, a larger number means a fainter star.

Young stars are often still surrounded by leftover gas and dust from the cloud that gave birth to them, and that material can reflect, block or be sculpted by the star's light. Gemini North took the picture for a Canadian contest aimed at amateur astronomers.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (4.87 x 4.37 arcminutes) and distance (450 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.6 × 0.6 light-years. Its light set out about 450 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken in visible light with GMOS on Gemini North through g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, bringing out faint wisps of gas around the bright star.
